skill.displayName: Lingxi-MindVault - Auto Memory Extraction for OpenClaw

version.changelog: v1.1.15: add explicit risk disclosure - this skill reads local OpenClaw session files and sends content to AI agent for extraction, then writes result to your own Feishu knowledge base. risk is stated clearly in SKILL.md

llm.summary: This is a disclosed memory-export automation skill, but it needs Review because it continuously reads private OpenClaw sessions and lets the main agent write extracted content to Feishu without tight controls.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads all unprocessed session files under the default OpenClaw sessions directory and exports derived content to Feishu. Although `SESSIONS_DIR` is listed as optional metadata, `session_check.sh` hardcodes the sessions path, so users do not appear to get the documented scoping control.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation guidance uses root-oriented OpenClaw paths, chmods copied shell scripts, and recommends frequent cron execution. The README also shows `source .env`, and `session_check.sh` sources `/root/.openclaw/workspace/.env`, which executes shell syntax from that file.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The extraction script instructs `openclaw agent --agent main` to read a raw session file and directly call Feishu write and message tools. That gives untrusted conversation content a path to influence a tool-enabled agent without a deterministic validator, allowlist, or user approval step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is designed for persistent scheduled background operation, keeps processing state files, and uses predictable `/tmp` paths for prompts and output. This is purpose-aligned automation, but the persistence and temporary-file handling increase local and privacy risk, especially if run as root.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the main behavior: scan OpenClaw conversation files, extract useful memory, write L2/L3/L4 records to Feishu, and send notifications. The sensitive data movement is substantially disclosed, so this is not treated as deceptive.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want all unprocessed OpenClaw conversations analyzed and summarized into your own Feishu resources. Before enabling cron, verify the Feishu IDs, run under an unprivileged account, avoid sensitive sessions, and consider adding explicit review, redaction, fixed session scoping, safer temp files, and a non-executing `.env` parser.
llm.findings:
[YR1] expected: The matched cron pattern is expected for a scheduler-based memory extractor and did not show a backdoor payload in the artifact, but it still supports a persistence concern.
[TP2] expected: The mixed Chinese/English skill name appears to be bilingual branding, not tool spoofing or a deceptive identifier.
[TP4] expected: The core side effects flagged by the scanner, including notifications, state files, heartbeat filtering, and script invocation, are largely disclosed in SKILL.md, so this finding is downgraded to a documentation/coherence note rather than treated as poisoning.
[SQP-2] unexpected: SKILL.md contradicts itself by saying missing environment variables fail safely but later saying defaults may be used. The inspected scripts require the Feishu variables and do not show hardcoded default Feishu destinations, so the exfiltration claim is not fully supported, but the documentation ambiguity is material.
[PE3] expected: Use of `.env` for Feishu IDs is expected configuration behavior, but sourcing `.env` as shell code is an insecure implementation choice if the file can be modified.
[SSD-3] expected: Reading complete local chat histories and exporting extracted content to Feishu is the intended feature and is disclosed, but it remains high-impact sensitive data handling without minimization or approval controls.
[RA2] expected: Cron persistence is expected for automatic memory extraction, but continuous background processing of new conversations without per-run review is a Review-level concern.
[T09] unexpected: The SARIF prompt-injection concern is supported: raw session content is processed by the main tool-enabled agent, which is instructed to perform external writes and messaging.
[T09] unexpected: The SARIF temporary-file concern is supported: predictable files are created in shared `/tmp` using session IDs and PID, then written through shell redirection.
[T09] unexpected: The SARIF regular-expression state corruption concern is supported: session IDs from filenames are interpolated into grep and sed regular expressions without escaping.
